artwork_craft.why: Frame 6 fails THE SHOWSTOPPER TEST, which caps this criterion at 6. With the type covered, the five mast blocks sit on a flat brown plane with no horizon, no dirt and no contact. At full size a set of dark slats rises in the air behind the AUSTIN block, which reads as a shadow artifact, and machine_qa warns that 'HOUSTON' is outside the safe zone. Frame 7 is also flat. The cyan beam stops at the eave and leaves a visible gap above the pod, the house has black-hole windows, and the figure is a mannequin. On frame 5 the dock reads as a post and a plank beside a faceless figure. Frame 4's top-down lawn, sphere and patio slab can't be parsed at 432 px. Frames 2 (the gridded suburb in haze under the aircraft) and 9 (low sun, open gate, box in the grass) are the only frames a reader would stop on.

deck_coherence.why: Two devices do real work across the filmstrip. The cyan line appears on frames 1 to 4 and 7, and the wood fence on 1, 3, 7, 8 and 9. Mostly dusk light holds 1, 2, 5, 7, 8 and 9. Frame 4 cuts to an overhead daylight lawn and frame 6 to a sunless brown void, and both sit outside the deck. panel_ready.txt contradicts itself: line 1 says the storyboard 'declares no value arc this gate can read' and line 11 says the deck is within one Munsell step of its planned arc.

claim_integrity.why: Every numeral I checked traces to a claim. 330 is c11/c19, 75 is c19, 63, 7.8, 8 and 8 are c13/c14, 220, 4,400 and 220,000 are c7, 36 and twelve are c34, 400 is c29, 59.7/63.5/65 are c21/c37/c38, and the frame 8 table matches c7's row quote. Both sources are primary FAA. Two problems stretch the source. Frame 7's dek says the draft 'caps delivery noise at DNL 59.7 dB', but c21 is a modelled finding ('would not exceed'), not a limit. The frame's own bar label, 'AT MOST DNL 59.7 dB', is the accurate form. Frame 7's kicker is 'THE DRAFT'S NOISE FINDING', yet the frame never states the finding (c26, 'would not have a significant noise impact'). A reader who sees two equal bars under 'At the draft's own line' is invited to infer the reverse of the draft's conclusion without being told what the conclusion is.

story_and_stakes.why: A Texan comes away knowing who (Zipline, FAA), where (the five metros, named on the cover dek and on frame 6) and when (October 11th). Frame 9 gives the exact action: the email address plus 'name the Zipline Texas Draft EA in the subject line'. That is the best thing in the deck. The stake it chose, how often an operator is sent an image (frames 4 and 9 and the caption close), is abstract to someone in Houston. The things that would reach their yard are in claims.json and not in the deck: 24-hour, 7-day operations with 5 percent of flights at night (c9, c10) and no setbacks for delivery points (c21 note). No county is named. The cover hook 'The pod checks the spot' tells a scroller nothing until they read the dek.

sequence_and_momentum.why: Frames 1 to 4 build as one descent: hover, lower, judge, hand to an operator. Frame 8 'Zipline prepared it' is a real late turn. Frame 5, the aircraft's dimensions, stalls the sequence right after the operator turn and could be cut. Frame 9's first sentence repeats frame 4's 'no figure for how often' word for word instead of landing somewhere new. The cover does not earn the swipe on its hook alone.

voice.why: The copy is clean and carefully attributed ('The draft says...' throughout), and I found no house-rule breaks in the caption or the slide strings. It stays flat and bureaucratic. Frame 7's dek is DNL jargon a feed reader won't parse ('the least added noise that lifts an area from 63.5 to 65 dB'). Kickers like 'The whole height, one block' and frame 8's 'The page sets passages from across the draft side by side' describe the deck instead of the world. The only Texas specificity is five city names.

variety.why: The subject (drone delivery, the pod on a line) and the dusk-over-fence palette look distinct. The rendered engine, the serif-over-sky layout and the mono furniture strip are house-mandated and shared with recent decks. I did not audit the last six ledger entries line by line. I read only the head of topics.json and am relying on the gates, so this score is weakly evidenced and not generous.

one_sentence_fix: Rebuild the cover and frame 7 around what reaches a Texan's yard: open on a 63-pound aircraft hovering 330 feet over a residential yard for about 75 seconds under a proposal to fly 24 hours a day (c13, c19, c31, c9) instead of 'The pod checks the spot', and on frame 7 state the draft's own conclusion (c26) with 'estimates at most' in place of 'caps' so the equal bars inform instead of insinuate.
other_findings: At the round cap with no hard fail, this ships at 6.36 by my reading. That is 1.64 under the 8.0 bar, and the email must say so. The deck is below acceptable, not a good deck.

Frame 7 (out/2026-09-24/copy.json S7 body): 'At that rate it caps delivery noise at DNL 59.7 dB at any point.' c21 says 'would not exceed', a modelled estimate. The bar label 'AT MOST DNL 59.7 dB' is the accurate wording, and the dek should match it.

Frame 7 carries the kicker 'The draft's noise finding' and never states the finding (c26). The two bars are equal by construction in compute.py, and with no stated conclusion a feed reader will read that as 'the deliveries hit the significance line'.

Frame 6 render: dark slat shapes float in the air behind the AUSTIN block (about 720 to 900 x, 950 to 1060 y at display scale), and machine_qa.json warns that 'HOUSTON' is outside the safe zone (55,777, margin 80 px).
Frame 7 render: the cyan line ends at about y 545 and the pod hangs at about y 570 to 640 with nothing between them. The line the whole deck is built on does not reach its pod on the noise frame.
Frame 2's floor label 'THE POD, ABOUT 75 SECONDS' sits at the end of the line, where no pod is visible at feed size, and reads as a caption for nothing.
Caption opener 'A pod comes down 330 feet on a line.' is supported by c19 (the pod is winched from a 330-foot hover to the ground). I checked it and it holds.
The cover cites c11, c17, c19 and c31, but no cover string asserts anything from them. They support the image only, which is allowed and worth knowing.
